_comment: Personal pronouns drawn as a picture, not searched for and not clozed (tunatale-3rxu, the user 2026-09-28). Each maps a word to a language-neutral concept in app.cards.pronoun_scenes.PRONOUN_CONCEPTS; the picture is a conversation with the referent filled and standing outside the outline, because a pronoun's meaning IS a relation between people and a photo cannot carry one. A word listed here is NOT a function word, whatever `function_words.json` or a POS tag says: app.srs.function_words.is_function_word vetoes it, so a PRON never goes down the case-marker cloze route. The veto is asked about a bare token, so listing a homograph would take EVERY sense of it off the picture route — the picture is therefore only drawn when the card's English gloss names the referent (app.cards.pronoun_picture.gloss_matches). Map only words whose MAIN sense is the personal pronoun. `kita` is NOT in `words` (tunatale-z4ya): its own sense in the user's deck is the verb 'see' (also the root of `kitaon`, 'let's'), so the inclusive 'we' is its SECOND sense in `senses`, keyed `pronoun`. Listing it here and letting the gloss guard separate the two stopped working once the verb card's gloss names both senses (the owner's R2): the guard would then draw 'we' onto the verb. kita is in no include list and Cebuano has no POS-based function words, so leaving `words` does not put it on the cloze route. `siya` maps to third_one and carries NO gender mark. `kita` is the inclusive we and `kami` the exclusive one, the same distinction Tagalog draws. The `_poss` words are the FREE FORMS of the possessive (tunatale-uy38): the same conversation scene as their nominative, with a bag carried by every lit referent, which is what keeps `siya` ('he/she') and `niya` ('his/her') two different words on two different pictures. `niya` is the gender-neutral 'his/her' and takes the third_one_poss picture, which is the only place the possessive says which referent it is: the gloss decides, since the scene is the same for all of them. `ta`, the enclitic of `kita`, is listed (the user, 2026-09-29), and was for a while the only card for the inclusive we. `mi`, the enclitic of `kami`, is listed too (the user, 2026-10-14: "Why does mi not have an svg?"): its card was minted with a Pixabay photo of 'we', and it shares kami's exclusive-we picture as `ta` shares kita's. Its gloss must still name the referent ('we') for the picture to be drawn. SHORT FORMS AND SENTENCES (tunatale-37c1, the owner 2026-10-16, from mockups): `ko`, `ka`, `mo`, `ta`, `mi` are all picture cards, and they were clozes or bare pictures before. A bare picture could not tell `ko` from `ako` (one referent), and a cloze could not say which of several pronouns its blank wanted. So each card's picture carries a SENTENCE with the word blanked, drawn under the scene: the drawing names the person and the sentence names the SLOT. `frames` holds one sentence per slot, and `word_frames` gives each word its slot. The sentence is the same on every card of a slot, so it never gives the word away. Long vs short is decided by slot (Wolff course 3 B 4: a predicate pronoun must be long; Tanangkingsing ch. 4, pdf p. 138: a topicalized pronoun is long only): subject = 'Moadto ___ sa merkado.' (Wolff Dict. mu- 'Muadtu ku didtu ugmà'; Bunye & Yap L12 'Asa ka muadto? Sa merkado.'); predicate = '___ ra.' for the long forms (Wolff Dict. kita 'Kita ra giyud way láin'); owner = 'Asa ang bag ___?' (the pattern of Wolff 'Anak ko', 'Pápa mu'; the owner accepted the sentence). The long genitives nako/nimo/nato have NO sentence: no slot takes them and refuses the short form, so the bare picture says 'the full word'. `senses` is a word's SECOND sense, a note of its own whose disambig_key names it: `ko`, `mo` and `ta` are each a subject AND an owner (Wolff: ku '{2} gen.: = nákù'; mu_2 'see ikaw'; nátù 'short form: ta'), and one picture cannot show both. The subject note keeps the word's own key, and its gloss names both senses, because its recognition card shows the bare word; the owner note's recognition card starts suspended (the owner's call; automatic since tunatale-ocv3). `kita` is the case where the first sense is not a pronoun at all (see above). `ka` and `mi` have no owner sense: nimo shortens to mo, and námù has no short form (Wolff Dict. kami). `glosses` (2026-10-14, tunatale-jm3d): the card gloss for a listed word, written by the pronoun table rather than the lesson's in-context gloss, which reached the deck as 'we' for kami/mi/ta and 'you (singular)' for nimo. Per language because Cebuano's genitive is also the agent ('by me'), which a language-neutral label would put on Slovene 'moj' too. `kita` has none: it is also 'see'.

glosses.niya: his / her; by him or her
